rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L68 "the Styling line from the digest setup" (chunk 5) is the closest; Send-it-off (included earlier at L64) line 45 writes that Styling line, so it is module-arc prior context. L87 "The door comes before the material" resolves against included what-goes-in (Phase 3 'Agree the door') per the module include-order carve-out.
L96 "On Day 2 the three of you read them" is a Next-slide forward pointer by name, not a positional callback; L68 names the Styling line by content, not by file position.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L72 "the moment you re-prompted three times" and "the door kept the interview notes out" are hypothetical examples of what a summary might skip, not 'the X you did' claims; door beat exists (apt101-what-goes-in.md:33 'Phase 3: Agree the door').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: not a demo beat: no guess-before-reveal or run-and-watch scene on any chunk

rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: chunk 0 L5 "Learn to do AI as a team, and stay in control of it." is one line but a self-carrying claim; chunk 8 L92 carries what to bring and why.

Closest: L38 'Start here' over a team question plus the module's lecture/exercise sequence; header is an orientation label and the content opens the day. L74 'Put the team's rules in one file' matches L76-80.

Closest: L40 "Not a disaster. The feature that shipped, worked, and quietly went unused." has a single 'Not X.' then a declarative, not 'Not X. Not Y. Z.'; L33-36 no repeated openers; no superlatives, no number+retraction, no verb triplet with an empty leg.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body grep for beat|mood|compendium|surface|firing|forcing returned no hits in lines 1-97 (L112-113 hits are in the maintainer block, out of region). 'door' (L87) is a coined term earned by the included exercise and used as plain vocabulary for the room.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L11 "**A laptop with Claude installed and signed in.**" bolds 8 words, over the ~5-word handle cap, on a prework bring-list whose bullets are checklist item names (handles); other bold: L12-14 item names, L40 label. Bold count per slide is a checklist, not a monoculture of lead sentences; filed as a suggestion only.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All ten chunks are the module file's own '##' sections (L3-L94), which reach the composed deck as section.module content; no phase-less prose section added. Not rendered by this judge; renderer contract is guarded by scripts/slides.test.js.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js -> 'OK — 55 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent.'; body grep for 'Phase N|Step N' in lines 1-97 -> no hits.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js <file> -> 'OK — 55 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut.' Only body hit is L12 "the three folders below made", whose referent (the make-the-folders prompt at L18) sits in the same chunk.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body has no inline links beyond standalone include links L42-L64 (structural, not in scope); review aid only.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file <file> -> 'slides: 10 limits: 210 words / 6 bullets oversized: 0'. Key Concepts (L82-88) sits at five bullets.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Headings L3-L94 are module-section names (Big Idea, Prework, Key Concepts, Next), orientation (Start here) or imperative labels (L66 'Write down how you worked', L74 'Put the team's rules in one file'); none is a declarative sitting where a label belongs.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L36 "Exercises over lectures. Cut depth where you need to." reads as design commentary, but it gives the room a permission to act on (cut depth) and is a room norm like its siblings L33-35; L84-88 Key Concepts bullets each recap one day beat rather than restating a doctrine twice.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No evidence of a rename: headers L38, L66, L74 sit over bodies that answer them (question + sequence; CLAUDE.md debrief; team-rules merge). Maintainer block carries no 'from <old-file>' provenance note.
